title: Rationalized Verdier data and coherence predicate
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. Use the coefficient categories, derived tensor and internal Hom, and constructible exceptional functors of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a coherent integral dualizing datum $w$ of [def-sf-coherent-integral-dualizing-datum], a rational Verdier datum consists of an ordinary integral tensor presentation with signed symmetry and the quotient-normalized ordinary-to-completed tensor comparison, preservation of integral constructibility, an exact additive $E$-linear contravariant equivalence on the raw rationalized category, its object and pure-tensor arrow formulas as the rationalization of the integral dual, and its evaluation and biduality with their integral localization equations. The rational conclusion predicate means that such data are supplied simultaneously for every finite coefficient field and every coherent integral dualizing presentation, together with finite scalar-extension comparisons rationalizing the integral comparison and preserving evaluation and biduality, with normalized identity and associator equations. The predicate quantifies over the supplied family and its comparisons; this definition does not assert it.
